summary: Implements bounded software batch-start control in linux/drivers/misc/idma.c. idma_submit is split into idma_submit_config(), idma_submit_commit() and idma_submit(). A new idma_batch_start() preconfigures A and V, then performs only ordered A-then-V NEXT_ID trigger reads plus ktime brackets and minimal commit bookkeeping under preempt_disable()+local_irq_save(). All IRQ/preempt restores occur before quarantine, poll, drain, logging, or resched. A zero ID marks A ownership, skips the V trigger, clears V batch_started, restores IRQ/preempt, quarantines A and leaves V clean. V zero after A keeps A ownership and leaves STOP/drain retention unchanged. Solo performs one V trigger with no fabricated A timestamps. idma_batch_window() now calls idma_batch_start() and preserves the existing poll/deadline loop. A new idma_batch_start_log() emits the frozen idma_batch_start version=1 dmesg contract once per batch round/session after observation finish, p4m_finish and e3_finish error aggregation. Nonbatch and controlled E3 paths do not use this helper and are not logged. Host tests are updated for the refactor and a focused batch-start harness/test is added.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compile and run the production bounded batch-start helpers against a host MMIO model.

This establishes software control flow only, not FPGA timing or hardware acceptance.
Only the production idma_batch_start/idma_batch_start_log helpers and their immediate
dependencies are compiled; kernel MMIO, ktime, HPM and userspace copies are stubbed.
"""
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
FUNCTIONS = (
    'idma_quarantine',
    'idma_submit_config', 'idma_submit_commit',
    'idma_batch_start', 'idma_batch_start_log',
)
CASES = (
    'order_both',
    'a_zero_skip_v',
    'v_zero_after_a',
    'solo_timestamps',
    'deadline_no_trigger',
    'signal_no_trigger',
    'irq_restore_paths',
    'log_contract',
)


def extract(source, pattern, label):
    matches = re.findall(pattern, source, re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL)
    if len(matches) != 1:
        raise RuntimeError(f'Expected exactly one production {label}, got {len(matches)}')
    return matches[0]


class IdmaBatchStartTest(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        cls.addClassCleanup(cls.temp.cleanup)
        build = Path(cls.temp.name)
        source = Path(os.environ.get('IDMA_SOURCE',
                      ROOT / 'linux/drivers/misc/idma.c')).read_text()
        definitions = '\n'.join(re.findall(r'^#define IDMA_.*$', source, re.MULTILINE))
        structures = '\n'.join(
            extract(source, rf'^struct {name} \{{.*?^\}};', name)
            for name in ('idma_device', 'idma_stream', 'idma_batch_start')
        )
        functions = '\n'.join(
            extract(source, rf'^static [^\n]*\b{name}\(.*?^\}}', name)
            for name in FUNCTIONS
        )
        harness = (ROOT / 'tests/idma_batch_start_harness.c').read_text()
        harness = harness.replace('/* PRODUCTION_TYPES */', definitions + '\n' + structures)
        harness = harness.replace('/* PRODUCTION_FUNCTIONS */', functions)
        (build / 'linux').mkdir()
        shutil.copyfile(ROOT / 'linux/include/uapi/linux/idma.h', build / 'linux/idma.h')
        (build / 'batch_start.c').write_text(harness)
        cls.binary = build / 'batch_start'
        subprocess.run([
            os.environ.get('HOSTCC', 'cc'), '-std=gnu11', '-O0', '-g', '-Wall',
            '-Wextra', '-Werror', '-I', str(build), str(build / 'batch_start.c'),
            '-o', str(cls.binary),
        ], check=True)

    def test_production_batch_start(self):
        for case in CASES:
            with self.subTest(case=case):
                result = subprocess.run([str(self.binary), case], capture_output=True,
                                        text=True, timeout=5)
                self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout + result.stderr)
                self.assertIn('PASS ' + case, result.stdout)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

critical_review_map.linux/drivers/misc/idma.c:idma_batch_sta: Core IRQ/preempt-protected A-then-V trigger. Review exact restore order on A-zero, V-zero, deadline/signal precheck and success. Confirm no sleeping, no poll/drain/quarantine/log inside protected section. Confirm A-zero clears V batch_started and diagnostic launch fields before later STOP/collect/cleanup. Confirm V-zero preserves A in_flight and A batch_started.
critical_review_map.linux/drivers/misc/idma.c:idma_submit_co: Extracted from idma_submit. Verify identical MMIO config order and diagnostic launch_begin_ns timing.
Extracted from idma_submit. Verify transfer_id/deadline/in_flight/next_offset/refill stats semantics are byte-for-byte equivalent to the old inline code.
critical_review_map.linux/drivers/misc/idma.c:idma_batch_win: Now calls idma_batch_start then preserves the original poll/deadline/cond_resched loop. Verify V deadline override and end_ns behavior on early trigger failure.
critical_review_map.linux/drivers/misc/idma.c:idma_run_sessi: Verify batch_start fields are initialized before stream_prepare failure paths, reset per round, and logged only after observation_finish/p4m_finish/e3_finish and final ret aggregation. Verify P4M and legacy batch log via else-if while E3 pair logs inside the pair block and controlled E3 does not log.
critical_review_map.tests/idma_batch_start_harness.c: Host model only. Verify IRQ/preempt depth assertions and MMIO order checks are not accidentally passing due to stub simplification.
critical_review_map.tests/idma_scheduler_harness.c: Minimal refactor stubs. Verify dev_info ignores idma_batch_start without changing existing expected obs_reports counts.

checks: Manual kernel build after applying: make -C linux M=drivers/misc modules (or equivalent source-pinned build command)
risks: IRQ/preempt protection uses preempt_disable() + local_irq_save(). The protected section is non-sleeping and bounded to trigger reads, ktime reads and commit assignments. Any future addition to this section must preserve that constraint.

A-zero path clears V batch_started and V diagnostic launch fields after IRQ/preempt restore and before V can be stopped/collected by the ordinary batch cleanup. If a future change makes V batch_started observable earlier, V could be quarantined incorrectly.

The log places a_to_v_ns as valid when both A and V NEXT_ID reads were attempted, including V returning zero. This is intentional under the frozen contract; consumers must read a_id/v_id to distinguish zero-ID failure.

idma_batch_start_log is emitted for legacy batch, P4M and finite E3 pair because they share idma_run_session batch mode. Controlled E3 does not use this helper and is not logged. This must be confirmed by Codex against the intended scope.
Host tests are software control-flow tests only. They do not prove FPGA timing, IOTLB behavior, cache coherency or interrupt latency.
The existing scheduler harness stubs local_irq_save/restore as no-ops. The focused batch-start harness models IRQ depth, but neither test is real kernel IRQ/preempt validation.

fields: a_id=<raw A NEXT_ID readback, zero on failure>
v_id=<raw V NEXT_ID readback, zero on failure>
a_begin_ns=<software ktime before A trigger, 0 if not attempted>
a_end_ns=<software ktime after A trigger, 0 if not attempted>
v_begin_ns=<software ktime before V trigger, 0 if not attempted>
v_end_ns=<software ktime after V trigger, 0 if not attempted>
irq_span_ns=<software ktime bracket lower bound; real IRQ-off extends a few instructions on both sides>
a_to_v_ns=<v_begin_ns - a_begin_ns when both A and V trigger reads were attempted; otherwise 0>
error=<final session numeric error, 0 on success>
log_contract.semantics: a_triggered/v_triggered mean the corresponding NEXT_ID read was executed, not that a nonzero ID was returned. A zero readback still sets the trigger flag and records a_id/v_id=0. The line is emitted only after observation finish, P4M finish, or E3 pair finish and final error aggregation. It is emitted for legacy batch, P4M and finite E3 pair that use idma_run_session batch mode; it is not emitted for nonbatch idma_run_experiment or controlled E3. Timestamps are software ktime brackets and are not hardware issue/cycle-accurate/interrupt-latency evidence.
